label: USE CASE 14
title: How UPI and Card Fraud Detection Works

scenes.text: You pay 50 rupees for chai, and it goes through instantly. [1] But if a stranger tries to use your card at 3 AM in another country, it's blocked in milliseconds. [2] Let's break down how fraud detection works.

Here's what happens in the second you pay. [1] You tap pay. [2] The system gathers the details, the amount, time, location, device, and who you're paying. [3] A model compares this with your normal behaviour, [4] and gives it a risk score, from safe to suspicious. [5] Low risk goes through, while high risk is blocked, or you're asked to confirm.

The key idea is anomaly detection. [1] The model learns what normal looks like for you, and flags anything unusual. [2] Like a huge amount, far above your usual, [3] a new phone, or a new city, [4] or many payments in just a few minutes.

data.definition: Learning what normal looks like, then flagging anything unusual.

scenes.text: Let's compare. [1] Here's your normal, against something suspicious. [2] Amount, your usual small payments, versus a sudden 80 thousand rupees. [3] Place, your city, versus another country. [4] Time, daytime, versus 3 AM. [5] And device, your own phone, versus a brand new one.

Banks use the learning types from episode 24. [1] Supervised models learn from past cases, already marked fraud or genuine. [2] Unsupervised models spot brand new tricks that nobody has labelled yet. [3] And rules add hard limits, like daily caps.

And there's a tricky balance. [1] False positives, blocking a genuine payment, which annoys customers. [2] False negatives, missing real fraud, which loses money. [3] Speed, because decisions must happen in milliseconds. [4] And step up checks, like asking for an OTP or PIN, when it's unsure.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think fraud detection means their money can never be stolen. [2] It catches most unusual activity, but when a scammer tricks you into paying yourself, it can look normal to the system. So never share your OTP or PIN, and never approve a collect request you didn't expect.

data.myth: Fraud detection means my money can never be stolen.
data.fact: Scams that trick YOU into paying can look normal. Never share OTP or PIN, or approve unexpected collect requests.

scenes.text: Quick quiz! A genuine payment gets blocked by mistake. What is that called? [1] Pause and think, and if you get it right, comment below! <pause 3.2> [2] A false positive! The system thought it was fraud, but it wasn't.

scenes.text: Let's recap. [1] The system looks at amount, place, time and device. [2] Anomaly detection flags anything unusual for you. [3] A risk score decides to allow, confirm or block.
